findings.title: page_count off-by-one error
findings.description: page_count always adds 1 extra page: `total // page_size + 1`. When total is an exact multiple of page_size (e.g. total=20, page_size=20) it returns 2 instead of 1, and when total=0 it returns 1 instead of 0. This will cause pagination UIs built on this helper to render a bogus trailing (empty) page. The correct formula is `(total + page_size - 1) // page_size` (with a total=0 special case returning 0 if that's the desired semantics).

findings.title: page_size accepted from caller without bounds checking
findings.description: list_expenses validates `page` but never validates `page_size`. A caller can pass page_size=0, a negative number, or an arbitrarily large number. SQLite treats a negative LIMIT as 'no limit', so page_size=-1 would return the user's entire expense history in one query, bypassing pagination entirely and enabling resource-exhaustion / excessive-data-exposure issues if this value comes from an API request parameter. An unbounded positive page_size (e.g. page_size=10_000_000) similarly allows a single request to force a huge result set. page_size should be validated to be a positive integer within a sane maximum, mirroring the existing `page < 1` check.

findings.title: page_count raises ZeroDivisionError for page_size=0
findings.description: Because page_size is not validated anywhere (see list_expenses), passing page_size=0 to page_count (e.g. from client-supplied pagination settings) raises an unhandled ZeroDivisionError instead of a clear ExpenseError.

findings.title: No tests for new pagination functionality
findings.description: The diff introduces count_expenses, page_count, and the new page_size parameter on list_expenses, but includes no test coverage. In particular there are no tests for the page_count boundary case (total exactly divisible by page_size, total=0), for count_expenses with/without a category filter, or for list_expenses with custom/invalid page_size values — precisely the cases where the bugs above would have been caught.
